name: Kaal Prediction Ledger
description: Dated, falsifiable predictions derived from claims in the Kaal Corpus, each with a stated resolution date and resolution criteria fixed in advance. The ledger exists so that when the field arrives at a position, the record shows when it was taken and on what reasoning. Predictions are never edited after publication; they are resolved.
author: Wulf A. Kaal
integrity_note: statement, made_on, resolves_by and resolution_criteria are immutable once published. Corrections are made by voiding a prediction and issuing a successor, never by editing in place. Prior states are recoverable from git history.

predictions.statement: In at least one deployed citation-weighted reputation system with more than 500 participating agents, the distribution of accumulated reputation across contributors will be heavy-tailed, and the top decile of contributors by in-citation count will hold at least ten times the reputation of the median contributor of comparable output volume.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Resolved CORRECT if a system meeting the size threshold publishes or discloses a reputation distribution satisfying both conditions. Resolved INCORRECT if such a system exists and the ratio is below five. Resolved UNRESOLVABLE if no citation-weighted reputation system reaches 500 agents by the resolution date, which is itself an informative outcome about adoption.

predictions.statement: No AI-agent liability insurer will consume a third-party, cross-vendor agent reputation score as a rated underwriting input. Underwriting will continue to rest on applicant-submitted governance documentation and audit results.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Resolved INCORRECT if any carrier, MGA, or Lloyd's coverholder writing AI liability publicly discloses, or is documented in a policy wording or rating filing as using, an externally operated agent reputation or trust score as a rating factor. Resolved CORRECT if no such disclosure exists by the resolution date. Captive scores operated by the insurer itself do not count; the prediction is about neutral third-party scores.

predictions.statement: The cross-organizational agent delegation mechanism that reaches production dominance will be operated by an incumbent identity provider or edge network rather than by a neutral standards foundation, notwithstanding that the specification itself is standardised in a neutral body. This is recentralization drift operating on the agent-identity layer.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Resolved CORRECT if, at the resolution date, the majority of measurable production cross-org agent delegation traffic terminates at infrastructure operated by a commercial identity provider or CDN. Resolved INCORRECT if a foundation-operated or genuinely federated registry carries the majority. Measured by published adoption data, vendor disclosures, or a documented survey; if no measurement exists, resolved UNRESOLVABLE and the prediction is reissued with a measurement method attached.
